deepdive.sec: PropTech — integrated real-estate operating system (discovery → distribution → transaction → managed living)

bull_bear.body: The dilution question was pressed hard and answered directly. ~20% incremental equity issued to REA (5% already held from PropTiger), taking REA to 24.9%. The founder's defence: dilution "affects us personally the most… we think about this very deeply every time," and both dilutions went to REA specifically — "the largest PropTech group in the world," owned by News Corp — for the intangible of global learning. He noted that in earlier acquisitions "we never diluted, but we diluted to REA." Valuation discipline is the stronger argument: Housing at ~1.5x revenue against listed marketplace comparables at 4.5x-10x, and PropTiger at 1x revenue now effectively 0.5x after the turnaround. A promoter-subscribed **~INR 200 cr war chest** is being created as insurance — "it's just good to have funds in the company… but I don't envisage to use this."
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Housing.com's losses are large relative to Aurum.** ~INR 200 cr annualised burn against a company generating INR 2.31 cr of continuing-operations PBT per quarter. If the four-to-six-quarter clock slips, consolidated profitability reverses.
- **Listing platforms have structurally failed to be profitable in India** — an analyst pointed to 99acres losing money for years despite heavy spend. Management's counter is that it monetises *past* the listing, but that is an unproven model at Housing's scale.
- **The reported profit is small and the quarter's real profit came from an asset sale** (INR 52.40 cr PBT from discontinued operations vs INR 2.31 cr continuing).
- **Culture/integration risk**, raised bluntly by an analyst: Housing has had "several mercurial founders… no one has been really able to control this company and they have burned money a lot." Management's answer — that REA has stabilised it over recent years — is reasonable but does not address integration of a much larger organisation.
- **Dilution:** ~20% for an asset that currently loses money.
- **Seasonality is now structural to reported revenue** — PropTiger's slab-based brokerage means Q1 is weak and Q4 is strong by construction; QoQ comparisons will keep looking bad in H1.
- **Deal not closed** at the time of the call; tax structure, unit economics and firm guidance all deferred to Q3/H2.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, unusually specific with historical numbers, and willing to be pinned down. The most credible moment was the founder voluntarily disclosing the gap between the public and internal targets — "Our internal target is three to four quarters; we are today saying four to six quarters… let's take it four to six quarters" — which is under-promising made explicit. He answered the hostile questions directly: how much has been sunk into Housing (INR 2,200 cr, ~INR 1,000 cr on brand), what the burn is (INR 200 cr annualised), why dilute (REA specifically), and what the mercurial-founder history means. The framing "our challenge is not getting 1+1=2 and making that profitable; our challenge really is how to make 1+1=3" is honest about where the difficulty lies. Weaknesses: no numerical guidance on revenue or margins for two-to-three years, the acknowledged deferral of tax and unit-economics detail to H2, and a general vocabulary of ecosystem/flywheel language that outruns the INR 2.31 cr of continuing PBT.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The quarter's profit is not the quarter's profit.** INR 52.40 cr of PBT came from discontinued operations (building sale); continuing operations delivered INR 2.31 cr. The margin expansion is real, but the absolute profit is thin.
- **The QoQ revenue decline is a feature of the PropTiger contract structure**, not deterioration — annual operating plans unlock progressively higher brokerage slabs, so value crystallises in H2/Q4. Expect this shape every year.
- **Aurum bought the one thing it could not build.** Everything downstream (Analytica for enterprise, Sell.do and Analytica for brokers, NestAway for living) already existed; what was missing was the earliest discovery signal, which only Google-scale search or a marketplace can capture.
- **The comparables argument is the real valuation defence** — 1.5x revenue against 4.5x-10x for listed Indian marketplaces, and a PropTiger precedent where 1x became an effective 0.5x post-turnaround.
- **REA sold the asset but took 24.9% of the acquirer** — as the founder put it, "it is not an exit which only fetches INR 458 crores… they have now 24.9% in the largest PropTech company in the country." REA is betting on the integration succeeding, which is a meaningful alignment signal.
- Housing follows a **July-June (ASX) financial calendar**, so its FY26 audited numbers will not align with Aurum's reporting for some time.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Proceeds from INR 112 Cr asset sale earmarked for full debt retirement and strategic reinvestment to accelerate AI-native PropTech transformation.
- No dividend policy or share buyback mentioned; focus on reinvestment and balance sheet strengthening.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Rental (INR 54.35 cr, profit INR 0.63 cr):** HelloWorld co-living, NestAway managed rentals, student housing and family rentals across 21 cities. **Both rental businesses achieved EBITDA profitability** — the stated milestone. Strategy is occupancy, tenant experience and operational efficiency "rather than simply expanding inventory."
- **Distribution (INR 55.94 cr, profit INR 7.97 cr):** Aurum Analytica (lead intelligence), Sell.do (SaaS CRM), PropTiger (brokerage). The profit engine, and always profitable.
- **Capital (INR 1.55 cr, loss INR 0.05 cr):** KuberX financing — sub-scale.
- **Housing.com (to be acquired):** marketplace model serving three customer types — developers, channel partners, and DIY consumers. FY25 revenue INR 343 cr against INR 531 cr of expenses (employee benefits, advertising, payment gateways, software/data). It has already discontinued certain services and divested PropTiger to Aurum.
- **PropTiger:** acquired from REA in July 2025 at ~1x revenue for INR 84 cr of shares; was loss-making, turned around, and has now delivered its **first two quarters of profitability** — the proof-point management leans on.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **The only end-to-end stack in Indian PropTech** post-Housing: discovery/listing → lead intelligence → CRM → brokerage → managed living → financing. The specific gap Housing closes is **top-of-funnel intent** — "the intent at the earliest stage of property discovery, which only two internet platforms get, one is of course the likes of Google… and second is marketplace platforms like Housing."
- **Brand asset acquired below replacement cost:** ~INR 2,200 cr has been invested into Housing over 14-15 years, of which ~INR 1,000 cr went into the brand. Aurum acquired at ~1.5x revenue against listed Indian marketplace comparables at 4.5x and, in one case, 10x revenue.
- **A demonstrated turnaround playbook:** NestAway (worse revenue-to-loss ratio than Housing, turned around), PropTiger (acquired at 1x revenue, two profitable quarters, effective dilution now ~0.5x), HelloWorld. Management's stated edge over tech-built businesses: "businesses that are built by tech teams… do lack that understanding on the real estate practice side."
- **Sell.do stickiness:** 7% gross churn with licences and developer count growing.
- **REA Group as a 24.9% shareholder** — the world's largest PropTech group, owned by News Corp — described as a source of global learning rather than just capital.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- India's only integrated PropTech ecosystem covering C2C, B2C, and B2B products across rentals, distribution, and capital.
- Transforming into an 'AI Native PropTech company' with AI pilots live across lead management, owner acquisition, and support.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [AI Roadmap] FY26-27 AI initiatives target 100% increase in lead-to-site visit ratio, 70% increase in call connection rate, 20% increase in lead conversion, 40% increase in site visit-to-booking ratio, 80% reduction in ticket resolution time, 50% reduction in inbound support call volume, 50% reduction in campaign go-live time, and 30% reduction in cost per acquired lead.
- [SM REIT Opportunity] Identifies INR 50,000 Cr+ SM REIT-able supply across India, targeting investors seeking alpha and income diversification through SEBI-regulated SM-REIT structures.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: PBT margin +1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margin +1,320 bps YoY, and management insists "these improvements are not the result of one-off cost actions; they are being driven by stronger business fundamentals, improved productivity, and disciplined capital allocation." Notably margins improved **1,000+ bps despite Q1 being "the industry's softest quarter."** The forward cost programme on Housing is specific: (a) internationally-invested, corporately-managed businesses "typically become management-heavy, top-heavy" versus Aurum's lean structure with frontline empowerment; (b) sales-team right-sizing on the broker and developer sides; (c) marketing efficiency — better use of credits on Meta, other social platforms and Google, disciplining performance/brand/SC expenditure; (d) working-capital discipline to cap expenditure. Aurum will also extend Analytica and Sell.do's enterprise team learnings into Housing.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q4 FY26 (prior):** targeting INR 1,000 cr annualised run-rate in coming quarters; profitability to improve QoQ/YoY on operating leverage and AI efficiency; distribution to compound scale in FY27; **SM REIT launch expected within FY27**; capital to be deployed into AI infrastructure rather than physical assets.
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** *Delivered:* third consecutive profitable quarter with PBT margin +1,590 bps and adjusted EBITDA margin +1,320 bps YoY — profitability improvement as promised; both rental businesses reached EBITDA profitability; capital continued to go to AI rather than physical assets (and a building was in fact *sold* for INR 112 cr). *Transformed:* the **INR 1,000 cr ARR target is now expected to be reached "a lot faster" and surpassed** because of the Housing.com acquisition. *New and dominant:* Housing.com acquisition announced — ~20% incremental dilution to REA (taking REA to 24.9%), acquired at ~1.5x revenue, currently burning ~INR 200 cr annualised, **committed to break even in four to six quarters** (internal target three to four). *Not mentioned this quarter:* the **SM REIT launch** guided for FY27 in Q4 FY26 — no update was given, flag for follow-up. *Deferred:* tax structure and effective tax rate to Q3/H2; Housing segment unit economics to post-closing.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: (a) has the Housing.com transaction actually closed and when does the breakeven clock start, (b) any update on the SM REIT launch promised for FY27, (c) continuing-operations PBT excluding asset-sale gains, (d) Housing FY26 audited numbers once public, (e) whether Q2 revenue recovers from the PropTiger slab seasonality, (f) the promised Q3 articulation of tax structure and carry-forward loss runway, (g) whether the INR 200 cr promoter war chest is drawn._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Housing.com to break even within four to six quarters** — the public commitment. The internal target is **three to four quarters**; management explicitly said "for this call, let's take it four to six quarters," adding one or two extra quarters because Housing is larger scale with more synergy opportunities. Reiterated three separate times by three different executives.
- **Housing.com current burn: ~INR 200 cr annualised.** FY25 reference: revenue INR 343 cr, expenses INR 531 cr. FY26 numbers are still being audited (Housing follows a July-June ASX calendar) and will be public "in the next few quarters."
- **INR 1,000 cr ARR target: "we're going to achieve that a lot faster with Housing.com transaction and surpass it a lot more."** No date given.
- **Company-level profitability including Housing: possible "over the next two or three quarters"** — because existing businesses are already profitable — but explicitly caveated as guidance to be firmed up after the transaction closes.
- **Tax structure / effective tax rate: "We will be able to articulate our clear positions in Q3, starting H2."** Carry-forward loss runway not disclosed.
- **Housing unit economics by segment: "Once we approach more towards the closing, we'll refine our thought process and also be able to give better numbers."**
- **Revenue/EBITDA guidance for the next 2-3 years: explicitly declined.** "I'll not be able to give you an exact guidance in terms of what do we see in numbers, but… the growth is what we have showcased over the last five years, we're going to go beyond that growth trajectory as well."
- **Priorities for the rest of FY27:** consistent improvement in financial metrics every quarter; continued AI progress every week; full integration of Housing.com synergies as soon as possible.
- **Promoter war chest: ~INR 200 cr** to be subscribed — "but I don't envisage to use this."
- **Dilution: ~20% incremental** to REA Group (5% already held from the PropTiger deal), taking REA to **24.9%**.
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
Not applicable in the classic sense. The pipeline metrics disclosed:
- **Housing.com:** ~24% of India's online portal market; **58 mn average monthly visits, 12 mn monthly active app users**; app leadership position over other portals.
- **Sell.do:** 1,000+ developers onboarded, **11,800+ active licences**, gross churn **7%** for FY26 — described as "extremely high customer retention."
- **Distribution reach:** 1,200+ developers, 1,50,000 projects, 40+ cities.
- **Rental:** 81% occupancy across 21 cities; customer rating 4.3.
- **TAM framing:** ~2.5 crore property transactions annually in India, of which ~1.2 crore expected to become digitally addressable; only 7-10 lakh residential transactions currently intermediated online. Annual residential transaction value >INR 15,00,000 cr, with ~INR 38,000 cr spent annually on property marketing and mortgage — of which **online portals capture only ~INR 1,200 cr, less than 5% penetration.**
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **The monetisation thesis:** "Traditionally, property portals monetize listings and advertisements; our monetization begins when the portals end." Housing.com captures consumer intent; Aurum monetises it through developer technology, transaction fulfilment, rentals, financing and AI-enabled services across the whole consumer journey — expanding consumer lifetime value and capturing a larger share of each transaction's economics.
- **Three named revenue levers on Housing:** (1) convert intent-monetisation into transaction-monetisation across developers, brokers and DIY; (2) upsell existing Housing product SKUs, which management says have good tech but "minimal utilisation"; (3) ancillary cross-sell — Housing × PropTiger, Housing × Sell.do, Housing × NestAway/HelloWorld.
- **AI across five layers** — Discovery, Intelligence, Transaction, Financing, Living — with **revenue per team member** as the tracked productivity metric. Medium-term goal is "Aurum's Unified Brain," a single intelligence layer activating monetisation across the ecosystem.
- **Industry consolidation:** "Aurum's acquisition of Housing.com marks the start of industry-wide consolidation in Indian PropTech, and at Aurum, we intend to lead it."
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Aurum PropTech achieved its second consecutive profitable quarter (Q4 FY26) with INR 123.85 Cr revenue , confirming structural profitability driven by high-margin distribution  offsetting rental rationalization. The sale of non-strategic buildings will render the company debt-free by June 2026, freeing capital for an aggressive 'AI-First' transformation aimed at boosting revenue per employee and launching a commercial SM REIT in FY27.
